sph_interpretive_translation: Those who have renounced worldly life, those in the stage of vanaprastha, those who follow disciplined celibacy, and those who share the inheritance of truth shall be honored according to their sequential spiritual standing—teacher, disciple, brother in dharma, and co-traveler on the path.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derived from spiritual succession, not temporal power
Causation through conscious alignment with dharma
Capacity-based responsibility determined by stage of realization
Restoration logic rooted in honoring spiritual hierarchy
Consciousness alignment through recognition of spiritual roles
executable_legal_axioms: IF actor is in vanaprastha stage THEN assign precedence in spiritual discourse
IF actor is brahmacari THEN ensure environment supports vow integrity
IF two parties claim inheritance of truth THEN rank by teacher-disciple lineage
IF conflict arises among equals THEN resolve via shared tirtha status verification
IF capacity is disputed THEN evaluate based on adherence to dharma-role sequence
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, precedence shall be given to those whose lives embody successive stages of sannyasa and dharma. Legal standing must reflect spiritual authenticity verified through lineage and practice, not institutional position alone.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Truth unfolds sequentially through pramana-based recognition of spiritual maturity. Each role carries inherent dharma that aligns naturally when properly sequenced. Responsibility flows from clarity of vision, not imposition of consequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Reaffirmation of spiritual hierarchy through ceremonial acknowledgment
Reallocation of duties to match current stage of sadhana
Guided reintegration into appropriate sangha structures
Removal of external pressures disrupting natural dharmic progression
Establishment of guru-shishya connection where disruption occurred
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands as Sanatana Dharma — sourced in pure consciousness, executed without punishment, restored through alignment, and judged only by the Self.
